item.title: In the wake of Spokane wildfires, preparedness experts think it could've been worse
item.description: As emergency responders in Spokane take stock of the damages from devastating wildfires, there's a prevailing sense that this disaster could have been far worse.

item.title: A look at 'Operation Country Roads,' West Virginia's ICE operation
item.description: Earlier this year ICE arrested 600 immigrants over a two week period. Most migrants had no criminal records and, since then, West Virginia has decided to not hold ICE detainees in their jails. A look at West Virginia post Operation Country Roads.

item.title: The park service says Trump's arch would obstruct historic sites. Could it be moved?
item.description: President Trump's proposed arch in Memorial Circle would intrude on dozens of nearby sites, says the National Park Service. But there's been minimal discussion of alternate locations.

item.title: Trump administration moves to deregulate Head Start, opening door for sweeping change
item.description: It would slim regulation of the 60-year-old anti-poverty program and aim to save money. Advocates worry the changes could undermine the early education program's mission.

item.description: The firm, Houston-based Burke Law Group has only two attorneys who specialize in immigration and asylum cases. Two of its founders have ties to the Trump administration.

item.title: Judge reluctantly dismisses case against Oath Keepers militia group over Jan. 6 riot
item.description: A judge has granted the Justice Department's bid to drop a landmark case against leaders of the Oath Keepers, as former prosecutors warn about the dangers of denying the violence of Jan. 6.

item.title: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan's Democratic primary for Senate
item.description: El-Sayed, an epidemiologist, backs Medicare for all and decries corporate money in politics. He beat Rep. Haley Stevens, whose supporters said she would have had a better chance in the fall.
